A parabola changes direction exactly once, at its axis $x=2$. With a positive stretch the graph falls on everything to the left of the axis und rises on everything to its right.

$$p(x)=3x^{2}-12x+7$$

$$a=3$$

$$3>0$$

$$x<2$$

$$p\text{ is decreasing}$$

The half-line $x<2$ lies entirely on the decreasing side of the axis.

$p$ is decreasing für every $x<2$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.61.solution_overview:
A single quadratic rule carries every claim.

$$p(x)=3x^{2}-12x+7$$

Two standard readings cover most of what follows: the vertex von the completed square, und the sum und product of the roots von the coefficients.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(2,-5\right),\qquad S = 4,\qquad P = \frac{7}{3}
$$

A positive discriminant puts two crossings on the $x$-axis.

$$\Delta=60$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-5$.

MATH 7.62.title: Ticketpreis gegen Wochenumsatz
MATH 7.62.context: A small cinema models its weekly revenue in euros at a ticket price of $x$ euros by $R(x)=-2x^{2}+36x$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: The weekly revenue is largest at $x=9$.
The largest possible weekly revenue equals $162$ euros.
The weekly revenue is zero exactly at $x=0$ und $x=18$.
Between $x=2$ und $x=6$ the weekly revenue changes at an average rate of $16$ euros per unit of $x$.
At $x=10$ the weekly revenue equals $160$ euros.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Weekly revenue follows a parabola, so the best ticket price is the abscissa of the Extrempunkt, read von the first two coefficients.

$$R(x)=-2x^{2}+36x$$

$$a=-2,\ b$$

$$a=36$$

$$x=-\frac{36}{2\cdot(-2)}$$

$$x=9$$

The Leitkoeffizient $-2$ is negative, so the model rises up to that input und falls afterwards.

The weekly revenue is largest at $x=9$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The extreme revenue is the height of the Extrempunkt, so evaluate the model at the abscissa $x=9$.

$$R(9)=-2\cdot 9^{2}+36\cdot 9$$

$$9^{2}=81$$

$$R(9)=-2\cdot 81+36\cdot 9$$

$$R(9)=-162+324$$

$$R(9)=162$$

Because $a=-2<0$ this height is the largest value the model ever reaches.

The largest weekly revenue is $162$ euros.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

Revenue vanishes where the quadratic is zero, so factor out the common $x$ von the given formula.

$$-2x^{2}+36x=0$$

$$-2x(x-18)=0$$

$$x=0$$

$$x=18$$

Those are the two zeros named in the claim, und a quadratic has no further roots.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

An average rate compares the change of revenue mit the change of the ticket price, so evaluate both endpoints first und then divide.

$$R(2)=-2\cdot 4+72$$

$$R(2)=64$$

$$R(6)=-2\cdot 36+216$$

$$R(6)=144$$

$$\frac{R(6)-R(2)}{6-2}=\frac{80}{4}$$

$$\frac{R(6)-R(2)}{6-2}=20$$

The average rate over that stretch is $20$, not the claimed $16$.

The claimed rate $16$ is wrong.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

Insert the ticket price $10$ into the revenue model und simplify term by term.

$$R(x)=-2x^{2}+36x$$

$$R(10)=-2\cdot 10^{2}+36\cdot 10$$

$$10^{2}=100$$

$$R(10)=-2\cdot 100+36\cdot 10$$

$$R(10)=160$$

$$R(10)=-200+360$$

The square term subtracts $200$ euros while the linear term contributes $360$.

The weekly revenue at $x=10$ is $160$ euros.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.62.solution_overview:
The story reduces to one formula und the quantities it links.

$$R(x)=-2x^{2}+36x$$

The axis formula fixes the Extrempunkt, while the sum $S$ und the product $P$ of the roots come out of the coefficients mit no equation to solve.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(9,162\right),\qquad S = 18,\qquad P = 0
$$

A positive discriminant puts two crossings on the $x$-axis, placed symmetrically around the axis of the parabola.

$$
\Delta = 1296,\qquad x_{1} = 0,\qquad x_{2} = 18
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach unten, daher ist der Extrempunkt der höchste Punkt des Graphen und der größte Wert ist $162$.

MATH 7.63.title: Quadratische Ergänzung mit negativer Konstante
MATH 7.63.context: Consider the parabola $q(x)=x^{2}+8x+10$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Quadratische Ergänzung liefert $q(x)=\left(x+4\right)^{2}-6$.
Der Scheitel des Graphen von $q$ ist der Punkt $\left(-4,-6\right)$.
Der kleinste von $q$ angenommene Wert ist $10$.
$q(x)\ge -6$ holds für every real $x$.
Die Symmetrieachse von $q$ ist die Gerade $x=4$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Die quadratische Ergänzung isoliert die Achsenverschiebung aus der Hälfte des mittleren Koeffizienten und stellt dann die Konstante wieder her, sodass die umgeschriebene Formel dem ursprünglichen Polynom entspricht.

$$q(x)=x^{2}+8x+10$$

Halbiere den mittleren Koeffizienten des monischen quadratischen Faktors.

$$\frac{b}{2a}=4$$

$$\left(\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2=16$$

Die Achsenverschiebung ist das Gegenteil dieses halbierten Koeffizienten.

$$h=-\frac{b}{2a}$$

$$h=-4$$

Werte die ursprüngliche Vorschrift an der Achse aus, um die Höhe nach quadratischer Ergänzung abzulesen.

$$q(-4)=(-4)^{2}+(8)\cdot(-4)+(10)$$

$$q(-4)=16+(-32)+(10)$$

$$q(-4)=-6$$

Setze Streckung, Verschiebung und Höhe zusammen.

$$q(x)=(x+4)^2-6$$

Das stimmt mit der behaupteten Form nach quadratischer Ergänzung überein.

$$q(x)=\left(x+4\right)^{2}-6$$

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The Extrempunkt is the pair (axis, height on the axis), both of which were just computed von the given formula.

$$x=-4$$

$$q(-4)=-6$$

$$\text{vertex}=(-4,-6)$$

The Leitkoeffizient $1$ is positive, so this point is the lowest on the graph.

Der Scheitel ist $(-4,-6)$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

The smallest value of an upward-opening parabola is the vertex height, not the constant term $10$ sitting at the end of the formula.

$$q(-4)=-6$$

The arms rise on both sides, so the values never sink below $-6$.

$$q(x)\ge -6$$

The smallest value is $-6$, not the intercept $10$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

An inequality that has to hold für every real $x$ is a statement about the vertex height. Completing the square makes the bound visible.

$$q(x)=(x+4)^{2}-6$$

The square is never negative, so the values never drop below $-6$, und $-6$ is attained at $x=-4$.

$$q(x)\ge -6$$

The bound holds für every real $x$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

The axis is the vertical line through the Extrempunkt, whose abscissa is $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$.

$$x=-\frac{8}{2\cdot 1}$$

$$x=-\frac{8}{2}$$

$$x=-4$$

Completing the square gives $(x+4)^{2}-6$, which opens on the same axis $x=-4$. The claim names $x=4$, the opposite sign — the same mix-up as reading $(x+4)^{2}$ as if it were $(x-4)^{2}$. The axis is $x=-4$ rather than $x=4$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.63.solution_overview:
Alles Folgende bezieht sich auf dieselbe Parabel.

$$q(x)=x^{2}+8x+10$$

Bevor du irgendetwas prüfst, lohnt es sich, den Scheitel sowie Summe und Produkt der Wurzeln aufzuschreiben — alles drei ist Koeffizientenrechnung.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(-4,-6\right),\qquad S = -8,\qquad P = 10
$$

A positive discriminant puts two crossings on the $x$-axis.

$$\Delta=24$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-6$.

MATH 7.64.title: Welches Modell passt zu den Messungen?
MATH 7.64.context: A meter reading was recorded once per minute für five minutes; $x$ counts the minutes und $y$ is the reading. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: The table is consistent mit a linear model.
Eine lineare Vorschrift durch die Tabelle hat Steigung $-3$.
The average rate of change between $x=0$ und $x=4$ is $-3$.
Die Tabelle wird durch die Vorschrift $y=-3x+10$ erzeugt.
Die zweiten Differenzen der $y$-Werte sind konstant und gleich $-3$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

List the five readings und subtract neighbours; constant first differences are the fingerprint of a line.

$$y:\ 10,\ 7,\ 4,\ 1,\ -2$$

$$\text{first differences}:\ -3,\ -3,\ -3,\ -3$$

The steps are all equal, so a linear model fits the table exactly.

The table is consistent mit a linear model.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Die Steigung von a line through equally spaced rows is one first-difference divided by the spacing of the inputs.

$$\text{first differences}:\ -3,\ -3,\ -3,\ -3$$

$$m=\frac{-3}{1}$$

$$m=-3$$

Every pair of consecutive minutes produces the same drop of $3$.

Eine lineare Vorschrift durch die Tabelle hat Steigung $-3$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

An average rate over a stretch uses only the two end rows: the change of the reading divided by the change of time.

$$y(0)=10$$

$$y(4)=-2$$

$$x=\frac{-2-10}{4-0}$$

$$x=\frac{-12}{4}$$

$$x=-3$$

On a line that average equals the slope, already found to sein $-3$.

The average rate between $x=0$ und $x=4$ is $-3$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

Substitute the claimed rule into the listed minutes; matching the intercept und the slope already pins a line down, und the remaining rows are a check.

$$y=-3x+10$$

$$y=0\mapsto 10,\quad 1\mapsto 7,\quad 2\mapsto 4,\quad 3\mapsto 1,\quad 4\mapsto -2$$

Every row of the table is reproduced.

Die Tabelle wird durch $y=-3x+10$ erzeugt.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

Second differences of a line are zero, because the first differences are already constant.

$$\text{first differences}:\ -3,\ -3,\ -3,\ -3$$

$$\text{second differences}:\ 0,\ 0,\ 0$$

They are constant, but the constant is $0$, not the claimed $-3$ (which was the first difference, not the second).

The second differences equal $0$, not $-3$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.64.solution_overview:
Die Tabelle ist der gesamte Aufgabentext; lies sie als Liste von Paaren.

$$\left(0,10\right),\ \left(1,7\right),\ \left(2,4\right),\ \left(3,1\right),\ \left(4,-2\right)$$

Die Eingaben sind gleichabständig, daher sind die Differenzen benachbarter Ausgaben das schnellste Diagnosewerkzeug.

$$\text{first}:\ -3,\ -3,\ -3,\ -3\qquad \text{second}:\ 0,\ 0,\ 0$$

Constant first differences mean a line, und the slope is one difference divided by the spacing of the inputs.

$$y=-3x+10$$

MATH 7.65.title: Eine negative Streckung behält die Nullstellen
MATH 7.65.context: A scaled factored parabola is written $p(x)=-3\left(x+2\right)\left(x-5\right)$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Die Wurzeln von $p$ sind $-2$ und $5$.
Der Graph von $p$ öffnet sich nach unten.
Die Symmetrieachse von $p$ ist die Gerade $x=\frac{3}{2}$.
Der Leitkoeffizient von $p$ ist $3$.
The two roots of $p$ multiply to $-10$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

A product vanishes exactly when one of its factors does, und the stretch $-3$ never vanishes, so the brackets already display the roots.

$$p(x)=-3(x+2)(x-5)$$

$$p(x)=0$$

$$x=-2$$

$$x=5$$

No expanding is required, und there are no other zeros.

Die Wurzeln sind $-2$ und $5$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The stretch in front of the two brackets is the Leitkoeffizient once they are multiplied out, including its minus sign.

$$p(x)=-3(x+2)(x-5)$$

$$a=-3$$

$$-3<0$$

A negative stretch sends both arms downwards, so the Extrempunkt is the highest point of the graph.

The graph öffnet sich nach unten.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

The axis sits halfway between the two roots, which the brackets already name; the stretch $-3$ does not move that midpoint.

$$x=\frac{-2+5}{2}$$

$$x=\frac{3}{2}$$

Expanding und using $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$ recovers the same line: $p(x)=-3x^{2}+9x+30$ gives

$$x=-\frac{9}{2\cdot(-3)}$$

The axis is $x=\frac{3}{2}$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

The Leitkoeffizient is the stretch in front of the two brackets, including its minus sign.

$$p(x)=-3(x+2)(x-5)$$

$$p(x)=-3x^{2}+9x+30$$

$$a=-3$$

The claim reports $3$, which drops that minus sign.

The Leitkoeffizient is $-3$, not $3$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

Multiply the two roots sitting in the brackets; the stretch in front does not change the product of the zeros.

$$(-2)\cdot 5=-10$$

The same product ist das konstante Glied divided by the Leitkoeffizient after expanding.

$$P=\frac{30}{-3}$$

$$P=-10$$

The two roots multiply to $-10$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.65.solution_overview:
Only one parabola is in play here.

$$p(x)=-3\left(x+2\right)\left(x-5\right)$$

Ausmultiplizieren bringt dieselbe Vorschrift in die Standardform, in der jeder Koeffizient direkt abgelesen werden kann.

$$p(x)=-3x^{2}+9x+30$$

Completing the square locates the Extrempunkt, und Vieta's relations give the sum $S$ und the product $P$ of the roots without solving anything.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(\frac{3}{2},\frac{147}{4}\right),\qquad S = 3,\qquad P = -10
$$

Because the discriminant is positive the parabola meets the $x$-axis in two points, und factoring recovers them.

$$
\Delta = 441,\qquad x_{1} = -2,\qquad x_{2} = 5
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach unten, daher ist der Extrempunkt der höchste Punkt des Graphen und der größte Wert ist $\frac{147}{4}$.

MATH 7.66.title: Eine Parabel mit der $y$-Achse als Spiegel
MATH 7.66.context: The parabola $p$ has the rule $p(x)=2x^{2}-18$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Der Graph von $p$ ist symmetrisch zur $y$-Achse.
The values $p(-3)$ und $p(3)$ are equal.
Die Wurzeln von $p$ sind $3$ und $-3$.
The two roots of $p$ multiply to $9$.
Der kleinste von $p$ angenommene Wert ist $-18$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Symmetry about the $y$-axis means the formula is unchanged when $x$ is replaced by $-x$.

$$p(x)=2x^{2}-18$$

$$p(-x)=2(-x)^{2}-18$$

$$p(-x)=2x^{2}-18$$

$$p(-x)=p(x)$$

Equivalently the middle coefficient is $0$, so the axis formula returns $x=0$, the vertical coordinate axis itself.

The graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Opposite inputs sit at equal distance von the axis $x=0$, so they must return the same height; compute both to see it.

$$p(-3)=2\cdot 9-18$$

$$p(-3)=0$$

$$p(3)=2\cdot 9-18$$

$$p(3)=0$$

Both values equal $0$. That is no accident: $p$ is an even function.

The two values agree.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

Set the given formula equal to zero und divide by the Leitkoeffizient $2$.

$$2x^{2}-18 = 0$$

$$x^{2} = 9$$

$$x=-3$$

$$x=3$$

Both values really make $p$ vanish, und they sit symmetrically about the axis $x=0$.

Die Wurzeln sind $-3$ und $3$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

Multiply the two roots just found, or read the product von the coefficients $P=c/a$.

$$(-3)\cdot 3=-9$$

$$P=\frac{-18}{2}$$

$$P=-9$$

The claim reports $9$, which drops the minus sign coming von the negative constant term.

The product is $-9$, not $9$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

With no $x$ term the Extrempunkt sits on the vertical axis, so evaluate the given formula there.

$$p(0)=-18$$

The Leitkoeffizient $2$ is positive, so the arms rise on both sides und the values never sink below that height.

$$p(x)=2x^{2}-18$$

$$2x^{2}-18\ge-18$$

Der kleinste Wert ist $-18$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.66.solution_overview:
A single quadratic rule carries every claim.

$$p(x)=2x^{2}-18$$

Two standard readings cover most of what follows: the vertex von the completed square, und the sum und product of the roots von the coefficients.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(0,-18\right),\qquad S = 0,\qquad P = -9
$$

A positive discriminant puts two crossings on the $x$-axis, placed symmetrically around the axis of the parabola.

$$
\Delta = 144,\qquad x_{1} = -3,\qquad x_{2} = 3
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-18$.

MATH 7.67.title: Eine Parabel aus ihren Nullstellen rekonstruieren
MATH 7.67.context: A parabola $p$ has zeros $-4$ und $2$ und Leitkoeffizient $3$; recover its rule before judging the claims. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: The rule is $p(x)=3x^{2}+6x-24$.
Die Symmetrieachse von $p$ ist die Gerade $x=-1$.
Der Graph von $p$ trifft die $y$-Achse in $y=-24$.
Der kleinste von $p$ angenommene Wert ist $-27$.
The two roots of $p$ add up to $4$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Two zeros und a Leitkoeffizient rebuild a parabola: the zeros fix the factors und the coefficient fixes the stretch.

$$p(x)=3(x+4)(x-2)$$

Multiplying the brackets out puts the rule in standard form.

$$p(x)=3(x^{2}+2x-8)$$

$$p(x)=3x^{2}+6x-24$$

The rebuilt rule is the one printed in the claim.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The axis sits halfway between the two given zeros; the stretch $3$ does not move that midpoint.

$$x=\frac{-4+2}{2}$$

$$x=\frac{-2}{2}$$

$$x=-1$$

The coefficient formula on the rebuilt rule $3x^{2}+6x-24$ returns the same line.

$$x=-\frac{6}{2\cdot 3}$$

$$x=-\frac{6}{6}$$

$$x=-1$$

The axis is $x=-1$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

The vertical intercept is the value at $x=0$ of the rebuilt product, which is the product of the two constant pieces times the stretch.

$$p(0)=3(0+4)(0-2)$$

$$p(0)=3\cdot 4\cdot(-2)$$

$$p(0)=-24$$

That is also the constant term of $3x^{2}+6x-24$.

Der Graph trifft die $y$-Achse in $y=-24$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

The smallest value is the height on the axis $x=-1$, because the stretch $3$ is positive.

$$p(-1)=3(-1+4)(-1-2)$$

$$p(-1)=3\cdot 3\cdot(-3)$$

$$p(-1)=-27$$

The arms rise on both sides, so $-27$ is the smallest value und there is no largest one.

Der kleinste Wert ist $-27$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

The zeros were given as $-4$ und $2$, so their sum is ordinary arithmetic; the stretch $3$ never enters it.

$$-4+2=-2$$

The same sum is minus the middle coefficient of the rebuilt rule $p(x)=3x^{2}+6x-24$.

$$S=-\frac{6}{3}$$

$$S=-2$$

The claim reports $4$, which drops the minus sign (or confuses the sum mit the gap $2-(-4)=6$).

The two roots add up to $-2$, not $4$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.67.solution_overview:
Two zeros und a Leitkoeffizient describe a parabola completely: the zeros fix the factors und the coefficient fixes the vertical stretch.

$$p(x)=3\left(x+4\right)\left(x-2\right)$$

Multiplying the two brackets out puts the rule in standard form.

$$p(x)=3x^{2}+6x-24$$

The axis formula fixes the Extrempunkt, while the sum $S$ und the product $P$ of the roots come out of the coefficients mit no equation to solve.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(-1,-27\right),\qquad S = -2,\qquad P = -8
$$

The discriminant comes out positive, so the graph cuts the $x$-axis twice, once on either side of the Symmetrieachse.

$$
\Delta = 324,\qquad x_{1} = -4,\qquad x_{2} = 2
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-27$.

MATH 7.68.title: Eine Gerade durch Steigung und einen Punkt festgelegt
MATH 7.68.context: A line $u$ has slope $-\frac{1}{2}$ und passes through the point $(4,1)$; recover its rule before judging the claims. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: The rule is $u(x)=-\frac{1}{2}x+3$.
Der Graph von $u$ trifft die $y$-Achse in $y=3$.
Der Graph von $u$ schneidet die $x$-Achse in $x=6$.
$u$ is increasing.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

A slope und one point determine a line: start at $(4,1)$ und walk along the slope $-\frac{1}{2}$.

$$u(x)=-\frac{1}{2}(x-4)+1$$

Expanding the bracket puts the rule in the shape $mx+q$.

$$u(x)=-\frac{1}{2}x+2+1$$

$$u(x)=-\frac{1}{2}x+3$$

The rebuilt rule is the one printed in the claim.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The height at $x=0$ is the intercept of the rebuilt line. Starting at height $3$ und walking four units mit slope $-\frac{1}{2}$ lands at $3-2=1$, recovering the given point $(4,1)$.

$$u(x)=-\frac{1}{2}x+3$$

$$u(0)=3$$

Der Graph trifft die $y$-Achse in $y=3$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

The rebuilt line is $u(x)=-\frac{1}{2}x+3$. The graph crosses the horizontal axis where that height is zero, so isolate $x$.

$$-\frac{1}{2}x+3=0$$

$$x=6$$

Substituting back gives

$$u(6)=-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6+3$$

$$u(6)=0$$

so it is a genuine zero und the only one, because a non-constant line crosses the axis once.

The crossing is at $x=6$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

The rebuilt line is $u(x)=-\frac{1}{2}x+3$, obtained von the slope $-\frac{1}{2}$ und the point $(4,1)$. Substitute $x=-2$ und simplify term by term.

$$u(-2)=-\frac{1}{2}\cdot(-2)+3$$

The product of two minus signs is positive, so the slope term contributes $+1$.

$$u(-2)=1+3$$

$$u(-2)=4$$

Der Wert at $x=-2$ is $4$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

The direction of a line is decided by the sign of its slope. The given slope is already negative.

$$u(x)=-\frac{1}{2}x+3$$

$$m=-\frac{1}{2}$$

$$-\frac{1}{2}<0$$

Because the slope is negative, every step to the right lowers the height:

$$u(0)=3$$

$$u(2)=2$$

The function is decreasing, not increasing.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.68.solution_overview:
A slope und one point are enough für a line: start at the given point und walk along the slope.

$$u(x)=-\frac{1}{2}\left(x-4\right)+1$$

Expanding the bracket puts the rule in the familiar shape.

$$u(x)=-\frac{1}{2}x+3$$

Zwei Zahlen beschreiben sie vollständig: die Steigung, also die Höhenänderung pro Einheitsschritt, und die Höhe über dem Ursprung.

$$
m = -\frac{1}{2},\qquad u(0) = 3
$$

Setting the height to zero locates the single crossing of the $x$-axis, und the sign of the slope fixes the direction once und für all.

$$
-\frac{1}{2}x+3 = 0\Rightarrow x = 6
$$

MATH 7.69.title: Wer gewinnt weit rechts?
MATH 7.69.context: A non-constant line $f$ und a parabola $g$ whose Leitkoeffizient $a$ is nonzero are given; no numeric data are supplied. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: If $a$ is positive, then $g(x)>f(x)$ für all sufficiently large $x$.
If $a$ is positive, then $g(x)>f(x)$ für every real $x$.
If $a$ is negative, then $g(x)<f(x)$ für all sufficiently large $x$.
There is a line whose graph stays above the whole graph of an upward-opening parabola.
If $g$ öffnet sich nach oben, then the difference $g-f$ is bounded below on $\mathbb{R}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Write $f(x)=mx+q$ und $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ mit $a>0$, und compare them through their difference.

$$g(x)-f(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

Subtracting a line never touches the coefficient of $x^{2}$, so the difference is again a parabola opening upwards.

$$g(x)-f(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k\quad\text{with }a>0$$

Once $x$ lies to the right of the larger root the difference is strictly positive und wächst without bound, because the square term outruns the rest.

The parabola therefore stays above the line für all sufficiently large $x$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

Winning the race far to the right says nothing about a bounded stretch near the origin, so a single pair settles the claim.

$$g(x)=x^{2}$$

$$f(x)=x$$

Here $a=1>0$ und the line is non-constant. Halfway between the two meetings the line is the higher of the two.

$$g\bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}\bigr)=\tfrac{1}{4}$$

$$f\bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}\bigr)=\tfrac{1}{2}$$

The difference $x^{2}-x=x(x-1)$ is negative on the whole interval between $0$ und $1$.

An upward-opening parabola can dip below a line on a bounded stretch.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

The same comparison works upside down: subtracting the line leaves $a$ untouched, und now $a<0$.

$$g(x)-f(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q),\quad a<0$$

A downward-opening parabola is positive at most between its two roots, so beyond the larger of them the difference stays strictly negative und falls without bound.

$$x\text{ large}\implies g(x)-f(x)<0\implies g(x)<f(x)$$

Far enough to the right the line sits above the parabola.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

A line staying above the whole graph would mean $g-f$ never becomes positive, so look at what that difference actually does when $a>0$.

$$g(x)-f(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q),\quad a>0$$

Being an upward-opening parabola, this difference wächst beyond every bound as $x$ increases. With $g(x)=x^{2}$ und any line $f(x)=mx+q$ the difference is positive as soon as $x$ is large enough.

$$x^{2}-mx-q>0\text{ for all large }x$$

Every line is eventually overtaken, so no line can stay above an upward-opening parabola everywhere.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

Bounded below means the values never sink past some fixed level, und für a parabola that level is the vertex height.

$$d(x)=g(x)-f(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q),\quad a>0$$

Completing the square isolates a non-negative square multiplied by the positive number $a$.

$$d(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k\ge k\quad\text{for every real }x$$

The number $k$ is attained at the vertex of $d$, so it is a genuine smallest value.

The difference is bounded below on all of $\mathbb{R}$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.69.solution_overview:
Es werden keine Zahlen angeboten, daher müssen die Schnittpunkte der Graphen über die Differenz $g-f$ in allgemeiner Form gezählt werden.

$$g(x)-f(x)=0$$

Gemeinsame Punkte einer Geraden und einer Parabel lösen eine einzige quadratische Gleichung, daher kann es nie mehr als zwei geben. Weit außen auf beiden Seiten übertrifft der $x^{2}$-Term jedes lineare Glied, daher entscheidet die Parabel, wer oben liegt.

MATH 7.70.title: Wann ist die Differenz noch gekrümmt?
MATH 7.70.context: A line $f$ und a parabola $g$ mit nonzero Leitkoeffizient $a$ are given; write $d=g-f$ für their difference. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: The coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $d$ is nonzero.
Some choice of $f$ makes $d$ a linear function.
Some choice of $f$ makes the coefficient of $x$ in $d$ vanish.
Verschwindet der Koeffizient von $x$ in $d$, so ist die Achse von $g$ die vertikale Koordinatenachse.
Was auch immer $f$ ist: der Graph von $d$ öffnet sich in dieselbe Richtung wie der Graph von $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Write $f(x)=mx+q$ und $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ mit $a\neq 0$, und expand the difference. Only the parabola can contribute a square term.

$$d(x)=(ax^{2}+bx+c)-(mx+q)$$

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

The line only ever touches the $x$ term und the constant term; the coefficient of $x^{2}$ is copied von $g$ und is nonzero because $g$ is a parabola.

That coefficient equals $a\neq 0$ whatever $f$ is.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

Making $d$ a line would require the square term to disappear, so ask which choice of $f$ could cancel it.

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

A line has no $x^{2}$ term at all, so subtracting it leaves $a$ in place; the only way to reach a zero coefficient would sein $a=0$, which is excluded.

$$a\neq 0$$

$$d\text{ still has a square term}$$

No choice of $f$ can flatten the difference into a line.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

The coefficient of $x$ in the difference is the gap between the middle coefficient of $g$ und the slope of $f$, so it can sein steered by choosing the slope.

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

Setting $m=b$ makes that gap vanish; the line $f(x)=bx$ is one such choice, und any other intercept works equally well.

$$m = b$$

$$d(x)$$

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(c-q)$$

One suitable line removes the $x$ term completely.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

A vanishing $x$ term in $d$ means $m=b$, und that condition concerns the difference, not the original parabola.

$$b-m = 0$$

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(c-q)$$

Take a concrete pair where this happens while the axis of $g$ is off the vertical coordinate axis.

$$g(x)=x^{2}+2x$$

$$f(x)=2x$$

$$d(x)$$

$$f(x)=x^{2}$$

Here the $x$ term of $d$ has vanished, yet the axis of $g$ is $x=-1$.

The condition on $d$ says nothing about where the axis of $g$ sits.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

The opening direction is the sign of the coefficient of $x^{2}$, so compare that single number für $g$ und für $d$.

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

Subtracting a line changes the $x$ term und the constant term only, so both graphs carry the same Leitkoeffizient $a$.

$$a>0$$

$$\text{both open upwards}\qquad a<0$$

$$\text{both open downwards}$$

The two parabolas always turn the same way, whichever line is subtracted.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.70.solution_overview:
No coefficients are fixed, so the letters $a$, $b$ und $c$ have to sein handled through the formulas that hold für every parabola.

$$
x = -\frac{b}{2a},\qquad g(x)-f(x) = 0
$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig. Common points of a line und a parabola solve a single quadratic equation, so there can never sein more than two of them.

MATH 7.71.title: Berühren am Scheitel
MATH 7.71.context: A horizontal line $f(x)=2$ sits next to the parabola $g(x)=x^{2}+2x+3$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: The graphs of $f$ und $g$ have exactly one point in common.
Dieser gemeinsame Punkt ist der Scheitel des Graphen von $g$.
At the common point the two graphs have the same slope.
The two graphs cross each other at that point.
The function $g$ has two distinct real roots.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Common points solve $g(x)=f(x)$, so bring everything to one side und see what kind of expression appears.

$$x^{2}+2x+3-2=x^{2}+2x+1$$

$$x^{2}+2x+3-2=0$$

The left-hand side is a perfect square, which can vanish only where the bracket itself does.

$$(x+1)^{2} = 0$$

$$x$$

$$x^{2}+2x+3-2=-1$$

A double root counts as a single point of the plane, namely $(-1,2)$, und there is nowhere else the two graphs can agree.

Exactly one point is shared.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The vertex sits on the axis $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$, und its height is the value of $g$ there.

$$x=-\frac{2}{2\cdot 1}$$

$$x=-\frac{2}{2}$$

$$x=-1$$

$$g(-1)=1-2+3$$

$$g(-1)=1-2$$

$$g(-1)=-1$$

$$g(-1)=-1+3$$

$$g(-1)=2$$

So the vertex is $(-1,2)$, which is exactly the single common point found von $g=f$. Checking the line: $f(-1)=2$.

The contact happens at the vertex.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

The line is horizontal, so its slope is zero. At a vertex the chord slopes of the parabola collapse to zero as well: a step of size $h$ von $x=-1$ changes the height by a square.

$$g(-1+h)-g(-1)=((-1+h)^{2}+2(-1+h)+3)-2$$

$$g(-1+h)-g(-1)=h^{2}$$

Dividing by the step $h$ leaves $h$, which tends to $0$ as $h$ tends to $0$.

$$\frac{g(-1+h)-g(-1)}{h}=h\to 0$$

Both graphs therefore have slope $0$ at the contact point.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

Crossing would mean the difference changes sign at the contact point, so track that sign.

$$g(x)-f(x)=(x+1)^{2}$$

A square is never negative, und here it is strictly positive on both sides of $x=-1$.

$$g(-2)-2=1$$

$$1>0$$

$$g(0)-2=1$$

$$1>0$$

The parabola stays above the line on either side und merely comes down to touch it once.

The graphs touch without crossing.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Falsch

Real roots of $g$ exist according to the sign of its discriminant.

$$\Delta=2^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 3$$

$$2^{2}=4$$

$$\Delta=4-4\cdot 1\cdot 3$$

$$\Delta=-8$$

$$\Delta=4-12$$

A negative discriminant leaves no real solution of $g(x)=0$. Completing the square says the same thing more directly.

$$g(x)=(x+1)^{2}+2$$

$$(x+1)^{2}+2\ge2>0$$

The lowest value is $2$, so the graph stays entirely above the horizontal axis.

There are no real roots, let alone two distinct ones.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.71.solution_overview:
Both rules are handed over mit numbers already in place:

$$
f(x) = 2,\qquad g(x) = x^{2} + 2 x + 3
$$

No work beyond reading is needed für the slope, für the two values at $0$ und für the opening direction, which is upwards here because of the sign in front of $x^{2}$.

$$
m = 0,\qquad f(0) = 2,\qquad g(0) = 3,\qquad a = 1
$$

Since the parabola is concrete, the vertex can sein computed once und reused: the axis first, then the height above it.

$$
g(x) = \left(x+1\right)^{2}+2,\qquad \text{vertex} = \left(-1,2\right)
$$

Vieta's relations read the sum $S$ und the product $P$ of the roots of $g$ straight off the coefficients, und the discriminant of $g$ says how many real roots there are to sum in the first place.

$$
S = -2,\qquad P = 3,\qquad \Delta_{g} = -8
$$

Common points are the roots of $f-g$, und that difference is again a quadratic, so its discriminant settles the count: one here.

$$
f(x)-g(x) = - x^{2} - 2 x - 1,\qquad \Delta = 0
$$

MATH 7.72.title: Das Quadrat hinter einer Datentabelle
MATH 7.72.context: The five pairs below come von one polynomial rule of degree at most two. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Die ersten Differenzen der $y$-Werte sind konstant.
Die zweiten Differenzen der $y$-Werte sind konstant und gleich $4$.
A quadratic rule through the table has Leitkoeffizient $2$.
Die Tabelle wird durch die Vorschrift $y=2x^{2}-3x+1$ erzeugt.
The $y$-values in the table are smallest at $x=1$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Falsch

List the five outputs von the table und subtract neighbours; constant first differences would sein the fingerprint of a line.

$$y:\ 1,\ 0,\ 3,\ 10,\ 21$$

$$\text{first differences}:\ -1,\ 3,\ 7,\ 11$$

The steps come in four different sizes, und they even change sign.

The first differences are not constant.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**B.** → Wahr

Differencing the first differences once more produces the second differences, which für a quadratic rule are constant.

$$\text{first differences}:\ -1,\ 3,\ 7,\ 11$$

$$\text{second differences}:\ 4,\ 4,\ 4$$

They are all equal to $4$, the value the claim names.

The second differences are constant und equal to $4$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

For inputs spaced by $1$, the constant second difference of a quadratic rule equals $2a$, so the Leitkoeffizient can sein read off the table.

$$\text{second difference}=2a$$

$$\text{second difference}=4$$

$$a=2$$

The Leitkoeffizient of any quadratic through the table is therefore $2$.

A quadratic rule through the table has Leitkoeffizient $2$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

Substitute the claimed rule into the listed rows; für a quadratic, matching three rows already pins the rule down, und the remaining two are a check.

$$y=2x^{2}-3x+1$$

$$0\mapsto 1,\quad 1\mapsto 0,\quad 2\mapsto 3,\quad 3\mapsto 10,\quad 4\mapsto 21$$

Every pair is reproduced.

Die Tabelle wird durch $y=2x^{2}-3x+1$ erzeugt.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

A claim about the rows of the table is settled inside the table itself: compare the listed outputs und see where the smallest one sits.

$$y:\ 1,\ 0,\ 3,\ 10,\ 21$$

The smallest listed value is $0$, und it appears at $x=1$. The neighbouring values $1$ und $3$ are both larger.

The $y$-values in the table are smallest at $x=1$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.72.solution_overview:
Die Tabelle ist der gesamte Aufgabentext; lies sie als Liste von Paaren.

$$\left(0,1\right),\ \left(1,0\right),\ \left(2,3\right),\ \left(3,10\right),\ \left(4,21\right)$$

Die Eingaben sind gleichabständig, daher sind die Differenzen benachbarter Ausgaben das schnellste Diagnosewerkzeug.

$$\text{first}:\ -1,\ 3,\ 7,\ 11\qquad \text{second}:\ 4,\ 4,\ 4$$

The first differences move while the second ones stand still, the signature of a parabola; the constant second difference is twice the Leitkoeffizient times the squared spacing.

$$y=2x^{2}-3x+1$$

MATH 7.73.title: Extrempunkt, Nullstellen und eine horizontale Sonde
MATH 7.73.context: Consider the quadratic $q(x)=x^{2}-10x+21$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Der Scheitel des Graphen von $q$ ist der Punkt $\left(5,-4\right)$.
Die Wurzeln von $q$ sind $3$ und $7$.
Der Abstand zwischen den beiden Wurzeln von $q$ beträgt $4$.
Der kleinste von $q$ angenommene Wert ist $21$.
The horizontal line $y=-4$ meets the graph of $q$ at two different points.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

The Extrempunkt sits on the axis $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$, so compute that abscissa von the given coefficients und then the height.

$$q(x)=x^{2}-10x+21$$

$$x=-\frac{-10}{2}$$

$$x=5$$

$$q(5)=25-50+21$$

$$q(5)=25-50$$

$$q(5)=-25$$

$$q(5)=-25+21$$

$$q(5)=-4$$

The vertex is therefore the point $(5,-4)$.

That is the point named in the claim.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Set the given formula equal to zero. The discriminant first says how many roots there are.

$$\Delta=(-10)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 21$$

$$\Delta=100-84$$

$$\Delta=16$$

A positive discriminant gives two distinct roots, und the quadratic factors as $(x-3)(x-7)$.

$$x=3$$

$$x=7$$

Die Nullstellen sind $3$ und $7$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

The two roots sit symmetrically on either side of the axis $x=5$, so their gap is the absolute difference of the roots.

$$|7-3|=4$$

The same gap can sein read von the discriminant without listing the roots:

$$\frac{\sqrt{\Delta}}{|a|}=\frac{\sqrt{16}}{1}$$

$$\frac{\sqrt{16}}{1}$$

$$\frac{\sqrt{\Delta}}{|a|}=4$$

Both routes agree. The distance between the two roots is $4$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

The smallest value of an upward-opening parabola is the vertex height, not the constant term $21$ sitting at the end of the formula.

$$q(5)=-4$$

The Leitkoeffizient $1$ is positive, so the arms rise on both sides und the values never sink below $-4$.

$$q(x)\ge -4$$

The smallest value is $-4$, not the intercept $21$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Falsch

The horizontal line $y=-4$ meets the parabola where $q(x)=-4$, that is where $q(x)+4=0$.

$$q(x)+4=x^{2}-10x+25$$

$$q(x)+4=(x-5)^{2}$$

A square vanishes at one abscissa only, namely the axis $x=5$. The level $y=-4$ is the vertex height itself, so the line touches the graph once instead of cutting it twice.

There is only one meeting.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.73.solution_overview:
Alles Folgende bezieht sich auf dieselbe Parabel.

$$q(x)=x^{2}-10x+21$$

Bevor du irgendetwas prüfst, lohnt es sich, den Scheitel sowie Summe und Produkt der Wurzeln aufzuschreiben — alles drei ist Koeffizientenrechnung.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(5,-4\right),\qquad S = 10,\qquad P = 21
$$

Because the discriminant is positive the parabola meets the $x$-axis in two points, und factoring recovers them.

$$
\Delta = 16,\qquad x_{1} = 3,\qquad x_{2} = 7
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-4$.

MATH 7.74.title: Kraftstoffverbrauch gegen Reisegeschwindigkeit
MATH 7.74.context: For a lorry cruising at $x$ kilometres per hour, the fuel used on a fixed route is modelled by $F(x)=\frac{1}{50}x^{2}-2x+80$ litres. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: The fuel use is smallest at $x=50$.
The smallest possible fuel use equals $30$ litres.
Between $x=20$ und $x=40$ the fuel use changes at an average rate of $-1$ litres per unit of $x$.
The fuel use is never zero.
At $x=100$ the fuel use equals $80$ litres.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Fuel use follows a parabola, so the most economical speed is the abscissa of the Extrempunkt, read von the first two coefficients.

$$F(x)=\frac{1}{50}x^{2}-2x+80$$

$$a=\frac{1}{50},\ b$$

$$a=-2$$

$$x=-\frac{-2}{2\cdot\frac{1}{50}}$$

$$x=50$$

The Leitkoeffizient $\frac{1}{50}$ is positive, so the model falls to that input und rises afterwards.

The fuel use is smallest at $x=50$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The extreme fuel use is the height of the Extrempunkt, so evaluate the model at $x=50$.

$$F(50)=\frac{1}{50}\cdot 50^{2}-2\cdot 50+80$$

$$50^{2}=2500$$

$$F(50)=\frac{1}{50}\cdot 2500-2\cdot 50+80$$

$$F(50)=50^{2}-100+80$$

$$50^{2}=2500$$

$$F(50)=50-100+80$$

$$F(50)=50-100$$

$$F(50)=-50$$

$$F(50)=-50+80$$

$$F(50)=30$$

Because $a=\frac{1}{50}>0$ this height is the smallest value the model ever reaches.

The smallest fuel use is $30$ litres.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

An average rate compares the change of fuel use mit the change of speed, so evaluate both endpoints first und then divide.

$$F(20)=\frac{400}{50}-40+80$$

$$F(20)=48$$

$$F(40)=\frac{1600}{50}-80+80$$

$$F(40)=32$$

$$\frac{F(40)-F(20)}{40-20}=\frac{-16}{20}$$

$$\frac{F(40)-F(20)}{40-20}=-\frac{4}{5}$$

The average rate over that stretch is $-\frac{4}{5}$, not the claimed $-1$.

The claimed rate $-1$ is wrong.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

Fuel use hits zero exactly when the quadratic has a real root, so compute the discriminant.

$$\Delta=(-2)^{2}-4\cdot\frac{1}{50}\cdot 80$$

$$\Delta=4-\frac{16}{5}$$

$$\Delta=-\frac{12}{5}$$

A negative discriminant keeps the whole graph on one side of the horizontal axis. The vertex height $30$ already sits strictly above zero.

$$F(50)=30$$

$$30>0$$

The model never returns a zero fuel use.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

Substitute the cruising speed $100$ into the model und simplify term by term.

$$F(x)=\frac{1}{50}x^{2}-2x+80$$

$$F(100)=\frac{1}{50}\cdot 100^{2}-2\cdot 100+80$$

$$100^{2}=10000$$

$$F(100)=\frac{1}{50}\cdot 10000-2\cdot 100+80$$

$$F(100)=200-200+80$$

$$F(100)=200-200$$

$$F(100)=0$$

$$F(100)=0+80$$

$$F(100)=80$$

The square term und the linear term cancel, leaving the constant $80$.

The fuel use at $x=100$ is $80$ litres.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.74.solution_overview:
The story reduces to one formula und the quantities it links.

$$F(x)=\frac{1}{50}x^{2}-2x+80$$

The completed square hands over the Extrempunkt, und Vieta's relations hand over the sum und the product of the roots.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(50,30\right),\qquad S = 100,\qquad P = 4000
$$

A negative discriminant keeps the graph entirely on one side of the $x$-axis.

$$\Delta=-\frac{12}{5}$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $30$.

MATH 7.75.title: Eine Parabel durch Scheitel und einen Punkt festgelegt
MATH 7.75.context: A parabola $q$ has its vertex at $(3,-8)$ und passes through the point $(1,0)$; recover its rule before judging the claims. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: The rule is $q(x)=2x^{2}-12x+10$.
Die Wurzeln von $q$ sind $1$ und $5$.
Der Graph von $q$ trifft die $y$-Achse in $y=10$.
Der Leitkoeffizient von $q$ ist $2$.
The horizontal line $y=-8$ meets the graph of $q$ at two different points.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

A vertex already fixes the shape up to one stretch factor, so write the parabola in completed-square form und let the extra point decide the factor.

$$q(x)=a(x-3)^{2}-8$$

Substituting the point $(1,0)$ leaves one equation für $a$.

$$0 = a(1-3)^{2}-8$$

$$a$$

$$q(x)=2$$

Expanding the square puts the rule in standard form.

$$q(x)=2x^{2}-12x+10$$

The rebuilt rule is the one printed in the claim.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

One root is already handed over as the extra point $(1,0)$. The axis is $x=3$, so the other root is the mirror of $1$ in that axis.

$$3-(1-3)=5$$

Checking against the rebuilt formula $q(x)=2(x-3)^{2}-8$: expanding gives

$$2x^{2}-12x+10=2(x-1)(x-5)$$

$$x=1$$

$$x=5$$

Die Nullstellen sind $1$ und $5$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

The vertical intercept is the value at $x=0$ of the completed-square form mit the stretch $a=2$ forced by the extra point.

$$q(x)=2(x-3)^{2}-8$$

$$q(0)=2\cdot 9-8$$

$$q(0)=10$$

That is also the constant term of $2x^{2}-12x+10$.

Der Graph trifft die $y$-Achse in $y=10$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

The stretch $a$ was forced by the extra point $(1,0)$. Substitute into the Scheitelpunktform.

$$q(x)=a(x-3)^{2}-8$$

$$0=a\cdot(1-3)^{2}-8$$

$$0=4a-8$$

$$a=2$$

Expand to confirm the Leitkoeffizient:

$$q(x)=2(x-3)^{2}-8$$

$$q(x)=2x^{2}-12x+10$$

The number multiplying $x^{2}$ is $2$. The Leitkoeffizient is $2$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

The horizontal line $y=-8$ is the vertex height itself, so meetings solve $q(x)+8=0$.

$$q(x)=2(x-3)^{2}-8$$

$$q(x)+8=2(x-3)^{2}$$

A square times $2$ vanishes at one abscissa only:

$$x=3$$

The line touches the graph once at the vertex instead of cutting it twice. There is only one meeting.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.75.solution_overview:
A vertex already fixes the shape up to one stretch factor, so write the parabola in completed-square form und let the extra point decide the factor.

$$q(x)=a\left(x-3\right)^{2}-8$$

Substituting the point $(1,0)$ leaves one equation für $a$.

$$
0 = a\left(1-3\right)^{2}-8\Rightarrow a = 2
$$

Expanding the square puts the rule in standard form.

$$q(x)=2x^{2}-12x+10$$

Completing the square locates the Extrempunkt, und Vieta's relations give the sum $S$ und the product $P$ of the roots without solving anything.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(3,-8\right),\qquad S = 6,\qquad P = 5
$$

The discriminant comes out positive, so the graph cuts the $x$-axis twice, once on either side of the Symmetrieachse.

$$
\Delta = 64,\qquad x_{1} = 1,\qquad x_{2} = 5
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-8$.

MATH 7.76.title: Eine Gewinnkurve mit zwei Break-even-Punkten
MATH 7.76.context: A workshop's monthly profit in hundreds of euros, when $x$ machines are produced, is modelled by $P(x)=-x^{2}+24x-80$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Der Gewinn ist bei $x=12$ am größten.
The largest possible profit equals $64$.
The profit is zero exactly at $x=4$ und $x=20$.
Between $x=0$ und $x=10$ the profit changes at an average rate of $14$ per unit of $x$.
At $x=2$ the profit equals $0$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Profit follows a parabola, so the best output is the abscissa of the Extrempunkt, read von the first two coefficients.

$$P(x)=-x^{2}+24x-80$$

$$a=-1,\ b$$

$$a=24$$

$$x=-\frac{24}{2\cdot(-1)}$$

$$x=12$$

The Leitkoeffizient $-1$ is negative, so the model rises up to that input und falls afterwards.

The profit is largest at $x=12$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The extreme profit is the height of the Extrempunkt of $P(x)=-x^{2}+24x-80$, so evaluate the model at the axis $x=12$.

$$P(12)=-12^{2}+24\cdot 12-80$$

$$12^{2}=144$$

$$P(12)=-144+24\cdot 12-80$$

$$P(12)=64$$

$$P(12)=-144+288-80$$

Because $a=-1<0$ this height is the largest value the model ever reaches; the arms fall on both sides.

The largest profit is $64$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

Profit is zero at the roots of the quadratic, so multiply by $-1$ und factor the resulting monic polynomial.

$$-x^{2}+24x-80 = 0$$

$$x^{2}-24x+80 = 0$$

$$(x-4)(x-20)=0$$

$$x=4$$

$$x=20$$

Those are the two break-even levels named in the claim.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

An average rate compares the change of profit mit the change of output, so evaluate both endpoints first und then divide.

$$P(0)=-80$$

$$P(10)=-100+240-80$$

$$P(10)=-100+240$$

$$P(10)=140$$

$$P(10)=140-80$$

$$P(10)=60$$

$$\frac{P(10)-P(0)}{10-0}=\frac{140}{10}$$

$$\frac{P(10)-P(0)}{10-0}=14$$

The average rate over that stretch is $14$.

The average rate is $14$ per unit of $x$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

The claim that two machines already break even is a substitution into the profit model.

$$P(x)=-x^{2}+24x-80$$

$$P(2)=-4+48-80$$

$$P(2)=-4+48$$

$$P(2)=44$$

$$P(2)=44-80$$

$$P(2)=-36$$

The true zeros sit at $x=4$ und $x=20$, so $x=2$ is still on the loss side of the first break-even.

The profit is $-36$, not $0$.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.76.solution_overview:
The situation is captured by a single rule.

$$P(x)=-x^{2}+24x-80$$

Two standard readings cover most of what follows: the vertex von the completed square, und the sum und product of the roots von the coefficients.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(12,64\right),\qquad S = 24,\qquad P = 80
$$

Two real roots follow von the positive discriminant, und the Symmetrieachse sits exactly halfway between them.

$$
\Delta = 256,\qquad x_{1} = 4,\qquad x_{2} = 20
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach unten, daher ist der Extrempunkt der höchste Punkt des Graphen und der größte Wert ist $64$.

MATH 7.77.title: Halbskalierte Faktoren und die Werte einer Parabel
MATH 7.77.context: Consider $w(x)=\frac{1}{2}\left(x+1\right)\left(x-7\right)$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Die Wurzeln von $w$ sind $-1$ und $7$.
Die Symmetrieachse von $w$ ist die Gerade $x=3$.
Expanding gives $w(x)=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-3x-\frac{7}{2}$.
Der kleinste von $w$ angenommene Wert ist $-8$.
$w(x)\ge 0$ holds für every real $x$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

A product vanishes exactly when one of its factors does, und the stretch $\frac{1}{2}$ never vanishes, so the brackets already display the roots.

$$w(x)=\frac{1}{2}(x+1)(x-7)$$

$$w(x)=0$$

$$x=-1$$

$$x=7$$

No expanding is required, und there are no other zeros.

Die Wurzeln sind $-1$ und $7$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The axis sits halfway between the two roots named by the brackets; the stretch $\frac{1}{2}$ does not move that midpoint.

$$x=\frac{-1+7}{2}$$

$$x=\frac{6}{2}$$

$$x=3$$

Expanding und using $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$ recovers the same line: $w(x)=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-3x-\frac{7}{2}$ gives

$$x=-\frac{-3}{2\cdot\frac{1}{2}}$$

The axis is $x=3$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

Multiply the two brackets out und then apply the stretch $\frac{1}{2}$; the function itself does not change.

$$(x+1)(x-7)=x^{2}-6x-7$$

$$w(x)=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-3x-\frac{7}{2}$$

Every coefficient agrees mit the displayed expansion.

The expanded rule is $\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-3x-\frac{7}{2}$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

The smallest value is the height on the axis $x=3$, because the stretch $\frac{1}{2}$ is positive.

$$w(3)=\frac{1}{2}(3+1)(3-7)$$

$$w(3)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot(-4)$$

$$w(3)=-8$$

The arms rise on both sides, so $-8$ is the smallest value und there is no largest one.

Der kleinste Wert ist $-8$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

An inequality that has to hold für every real $x$ is a statement about the vertex height. The stretch $\frac{1}{2}$ is positive, so the values never drop below the vertex, but they do drop below $0$ between the two roots.

$$w(3)=-8$$

$$w(x)\ge -8\qquad w(3)=-8$$

$$-8<0$$

The claimed bound $0$ is broken at the Extrempunkt.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.77.solution_overview:
There is one graph to study, und it is a parabola.

$$w(x)=\frac{1}{2}\left(x+1\right)\left(x-7\right)$$

Ausmultiplizieren bringt dieselbe Vorschrift in die Standardform, in der jeder Koeffizient direkt abgelesen werden kann.

$$w(x)=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-3x-\frac{7}{2}$$

The axis formula fixes the Extrempunkt, while the sum $S$ und the product $P$ of the roots come out of the coefficients mit no equation to solve.

$$
\text{vertex} = \left(3,-8\right),\qquad S = 6,\qquad P = -7
$$

Because the discriminant is positive the parabola meets the $x$-axis in two points, und factoring recovers them.

$$
\Delta = 16,\qquad x_{1} = -1,\qquad x_{2} = 7
$$

Die Arme öffnen sich nach oben, daher ist der Extrempunkt der tiefste Punkt des Graphen und der kleinste Wert ist $-8$.

MATH 7.78.title: Höhen eines Steins, jede Sekunde erfasst
MATH 7.78.context: A stone is launched upwards und its height above the ground is measured once per second. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Die ersten Differenzen der $y$-Werte sind konstant.
Die zweiten Differenzen der $y$-Werte sind konstant und gleich $-10$.
Die Tabelle wird durch die Vorschrift $y=-5x^{2}+30x$ erzeugt.
The $y$-values in the table are largest at $x=3$.
Continuing the pattern, the value at $x=5$ is $25$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Falsch

List the five heights von the table und subtract neighbours; constant first differences would sein the fingerprint of a line.

$$y:\ 0,\ 25,\ 40,\ 45,\ 40$$

$$\text{first differences}:\ 25,\ 15,\ 5,\ -5$$

The steps come in four different sizes, und they even change sign after the peak.

The first differences are not constant.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**B.** → Wahr

Differencing the first differences once more produces the second differences, which für a quadratic rule are constant.

$$\text{first differences}:\ 25,\ 15,\ 5,\ -5$$

$$\text{second differences}:\ -10,\ -10,\ -10$$

They are all equal to $-10$, the value the claim names.

The second differences are constant und equal to $-10$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

Substitute the claimed rule into the listed seconds; für a quadratic, matching three rows already pins the rule down, und the remaining two are a check.

$$y=-5x^{2}+30x$$

$$0\mapsto 0,\quad 1\mapsto 25,\quad 2\mapsto 40,\quad 3\mapsto 45,\quad 4\mapsto 40$$

Every row of the table is reproduced.

Die Tabelle wird durch $y=-5x^{2}+30x$ erzeugt.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

Compare the five listed heights und see where the largest one sits; the claim is about the table itself, not about a continuous model.

$$y:\ 0,\ 25,\ 40,\ 45,\ 40$$

The largest listed value is $45$, und it appears at $x=3$. The neighbouring values $40$ und $40$ are both smaller.

The $y$-values in the table are largest at $x=3$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

The next first-difference shrinks by the constant second difference $-10$, so add $-5+(-10)=-15$ to the last height $40$.

$$40+(-15)=25$$

The same height comes von the quadratic rule already identified.

$$y(5)=-5\cdot 25+150$$

$$y(5)=25$$

Der Wert at $x=5$ is $25$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.78.solution_overview:
Die Tabelle ist der gesamte Aufgabentext; lies sie als Liste von Paaren.

$$\left(0,0\right),\ \left(1,25\right),\ \left(2,40\right),\ \left(3,45\right),\ \left(4,40\right)$$

Die Eingaben sind gleichabständig, daher sind die Differenzen benachbarter Ausgaben das schnellste Diagnosewerkzeug.

$$\text{first}:\ 25,\ 15,\ 5,\ -5\qquad \text{second}:\ -10,\ -10,\ -10$$

The first differences move while the second ones stand still, the signature of a parabola; the constant second difference is twice the Leitkoeffizient times the squared spacing.

$$y=-5x^{2}+30x$$

MATH 7.79.title: Eine Gerade um eine Parabel rückgängig machen
MATH 7.79.context: A non-constant line $f$ mit inverse $f^{-1}$ is given together mit a parabola $g$. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: The inverse $f^{-1}$ is again a non-constant linear function.
The nested function $g(f^{-1}(x))$ is a quadratic function.
The nested function $f^{-1}(g(x))$ is a quadratic function.
The nested function $g(f^{-1}(x))$ always has the same roots as $g$.
The nested function $f^{-1}(g(x))$ always has the same Symmetrieachse as $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Write $f(x)=mx+q$ mit $m\neq 0$ und undo it by solving $y=mx+q$ für $x$.

$$y = mx+q$$

$$x = \frac{y-q}{m}$$

The division is legitimate precisely because the line is non-constant, und the result is again a first-degree formula.

$$f^{-1}(y)=\frac{1}{m}y-\frac{q}{m}$$

Its slope is $1/m$, which is a non-zero number, so the inverse is not a constant function.

Undoing a non-constant line gives another non-constant line.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Nesting the inverse line inside the parabola substitutes a first-degree expression für $x$, so expand the square und collect the terms.

$$g\left(f^{-1}(x)\right)=a\left(\frac{x-q}{m}\right)^{2}+b\left(\frac{x-q}{m}\right)+c$$

The square of a first-degree expression reaches $x^{2}$ und stops there, und the coefficient it produces is the leading one of the composite.

$$\text{coefficient of }x^{2}=\frac{a}{m^{2}}\neq 0$$

It is non-zero because $a\neq 0$ und $m\neq 0$, so nothing wegfällt the square term.

The composite is again a parabola.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

In this order the parabola is computed first und the inverse line is applied afterwards, which merely rescales und shifts the values.

$$f^{-1}\left(g(x)\right)=\frac{g(x)-q}{m}$$

$$f^{-1}\left(g(x)\right)=\frac{a}{m}x^{2}+\frac{b}{m}x+\frac{c-q}{m}$$

The Leitkoeffizient $a/m$ is again non-zero, so the square term survives the rescaling.

The composite is a parabola in this order as well.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

Here the inverse line acts on the argument, so a root of the composite is an abscissa whose image under $f^{-1}$ is a root of $g$; the roots get moved rather than kept.

$$g\left(f^{-1}(x)\right)=0$$

$$f^{-1}(x)\text{ is a root of }g$$

Take the simplest concrete pair und follow the bookkeeping.

$$g(x)=x^{2}$$

$$f(x)=x+1$$

$$S=f^{-1}(x)$$

$$S=x-1$$

$$g\left(f^{-1}(x)\right)=\left(x-1\right)^{2}$$

The composite vanishes at $x=1$ while $g$ vanishes at $x=0$, so the two root sets are different.

Substituting inside the parabola shifts its roots.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

In this order the line acts after the parabola, und an operation performed on the values can only stretch or slide the graph vertically.

$$f^{-1}\left(g(x)\right)=\frac{a}{m}x^{2}+\frac{b}{m}x+\frac{c-q}{m}$$

Both the leading und the middle coefficient are divided by the same non-zero number $m$, so the quotient that produces the axis is unchanged.

$$-\frac{b/m}{2\left(a/m\right)}=-\frac{b}{2a}$$

The composite has exactly the same Symmetrieachse as $g$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.79.solution_overview:
Everything is stated für a general parabola, so the reasoning runs on the structure of $ax^{2}+bx+c$ instead of on numbers.

$$
x = -\frac{b}{2a},\qquad f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x-q}{m}
$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig. Nesting two polynomials multiplies their highest powers instead of adding them, so a line inside a parabola still leaves a parabola. Undoing a line gives another line, so wrapping it around a parabola cannot change the highest power that appears.

MATH 7.80.title: Eine Gerade und eine Parabel spiegeln
MATH 7.80.context: A line $f$ und a parabola $g$ are mirrored by replacing $x$ mit $-x$: write $\tilde f(x)=f(-x)$ und $\tilde g(x)=g(-x)$. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: The graphs of $\tilde f$ und $\tilde g$ meet exactly as often as those of $f$ und $g$.
If the graphs of $f$ und $g$ are tangent, then so are those of $\tilde f$ und $\tilde g$.
Mirroring in this way can turn two meetings into three.
The parabola $\tilde g$ always opens in the same direction as $g$.
The parabola $\tilde g$ always has the same Symmetrieachse as $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Mirroring replaces $x$ by $-x$ in both formulas at once, so the equation für the common abscissas is transported by the same substitution.

$$\tilde f(x) = \tilde g(x)$$

$$f(-x) = g(-x)$$

Hence $x$ is a meeting abscissa of the mirrored pair exactly when $-x$ is a meeting abscissa of the original pair.

$$x\text{ solves the new equation}\iff -x\text{ solves the old one}$$

The assignment $x\mapsto -x$ pairs the two sets of solutions one against one, und a reflection can neither create nor destroy a meeting.

The counts agree.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Tangency is the algebraic statement that the difference has a repeated root, so mirror the difference und inspect its shape.

$$\tilde g(x)-\tilde f(x)=(g-f)(-x)$$

If the original graphs are tangent at abscissa $h$, the difference is a perfect square times its Leitkoeffizient.

$$g(x)-f(x) = a(x-h)^{2}$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=(g-f)(-x)$$

$$\tilde g(x)-\tilde f(x)=a(x+h)^{2}$$

The mirrored difference is again a square mit the same Leitkoeffizient, now mit its repeated root at $-h$.

The reflected graphs touch at the mirrored abscissa.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

Write $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ und $f(x)=mx+q$. The number of meetings is governed by the difference, und mirroring keeps that difference quadratic mit the same Leitkoeffizient.

$$(g-f)(-x)=ax^{2}-(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

A quadratic equation has at most two real solutions, so three meetings are out of reach; the correspondence $x\mapsto -x$ shows the count was preserved exactly anyway.

$$a\neq 0$$

$$\text{at most two solutions}$$

Two meetings stay two meetings under a reflection.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

The opening direction depends only on the coefficient of $x^{2}$, so mirror the formula $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ und read that coefficient off.

$$\tilde g(x)=a(-x)^{2}+b(-x)+c$$

$$\tilde g(x)=ax^{2}-bx+c$$

Squaring kills the minus sign, so the Leitkoeffizient is still $a$ und its sign has not moved.

The mirrored parabola opens the same way as the original.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

Reflecting across the vertical coordinate axis carries the Symmetrieachse along mit the graph, so compute where it lands.

$$\tilde g(x) = ax^{2}-bx+c$$

$$\text{axis }x=\frac{b}{2a}$$

The original axis is $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$, so the two lines are opposites of each other und coincide only when $b=0$. A concrete pair makes the jump visible.

$$g(x) = (x-1)^{2}$$

$$\tilde g(x)=(x+1)^{2}$$

In this example the axis jumps von $x=1$ to $x=-1$, two different vertical lines.

The axis is mirrored too, so it generally moves.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.80.solution_overview:
No coefficients are fixed, so the letters $a$, $b$ und $c$ have to sein handled through the formulas that hold für every parabola.

$$
x = -\frac{b}{2a},\qquad \Delta = b^{2}-4ac
$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig. Die Diskriminante zählt die reellen Wurzeln: zwei solange sie positiv ist, eine wenn sie verschwindet und keine, sobald sie negativ wird. Replacing $x$ by $-x$ reflects a graph in the $y$-axis, und a parabola survives that swap exactly when its middle coefficient vanishes.

Both graphs are reflected at once, so the question is always which feature survives a reflection.

MATH 7.81.title: Wie viele Punkte legen eine Kurve fest?
MATH 7.81.context: Three pairwise distinct points $P$, $Q$ und $R$ of the plane are given, no two of which lie on the same vertical line. No coordinates are supplied. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Exactly one linear function has both $P$ und $Q$ on its graph.
There is always at least one quadratic function having $P$, $Q$ und $R$ on its graph.
If $P$, $Q$ und $R$ are not collinear, then exactly one quadratic function has all three on its graph.
Infinitely many quadratic functions have both $P$ und $Q$ on their graphs.
A quadratic function und a linear function can agree at all three points.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Two points mit different abscissas determine a slope, und the slope together mit one of the points determines the whole line.

The denominator is non-zero because $P$ und $Q$ do not lie on a common vertical line, so this quotient is a genuine number; the intercept then has no freedom left.

Any line through both points must have this slope und this intercept, so no second one is possible.

Exactly one linear function passes through the two points.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

Three points mit distinct abscissas are always matched by exactly one formula of the shape $Ax^{2}+Bx+C$, but nothing guarantees that $A$ comes out non-zero.

$$A x_{P}^{2}+B x_{P}+C=y_{P},\quad\text{and likewise for }Q\text{ and }R$$

If the three points happen to sein collinear, that unique solution is the line through them, mit a vanishing square coefficient.

$$(0,0),\;(1,1),\;(2,2)$$

$$A=0,\quad B=1,\quad C=0$$

A quadratic function needs a non-zero coefficient of $x^{2}$, so in this configuration there is no quadratic function at all through the three points.

Collinear triples admit only a line, so the existence claim fails in general.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

The three interpolation conditions form a system in the unknown coefficients, und distinct abscissas make it solvable in exactly one way.

$$
A x_{P}^{2}+B x_{P}+C=y_{P},\qquad A x_{Q}^{2}+B x_{Q}+C = y_{Q},\qquad A x_{R}^{2}+B x_{R}+C = y_{R}
$$

Subtracting the equations in pairs eliminates $C$ und then $B$, leaving one value für $A$, after which $B$ und $C$ follow in turn; every step divides only by differences of the abscissas, which are non-zero.

$$A=0$$

$$P,\,Q,\,R\text{ are collinear}$$

Since the points are assumed not to sein collinear, the value obtained für $A$ is non-zero und the interpolating formula really is a quadratic one.

There is one such quadratic function und no more.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

Passing through two points leaves one degree of freedom, und it can sein displayed explicitly: start von the line through $P$ und $Q$ und add a term that vanishes at both abscissas.

$$g_{\lambda}(x)=\lambda(x-x_{P})(x-x_{Q})+mx+q$$

At $x=x_{P}$ und $x=x_{Q}$ the first summand is zero, so every member of this family contains both points, while the coefficient of $x^{2}$ is $\lambda$.

$$\lambda\neq 0$$

$$g_{\lambda}\text{ is a quadratic function}$$

Different non-zero values of $\lambda$ give different functions, und there are infinitely many of them.

Infinitely many parabolas pass through the same two points.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Falsch

Agreement at a point means the difference of the two functions vanishes there, so study that difference.

$$g(x)-f(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)\qquad a\neq 0$$

This is a quadratic expression, so it can vanish at two abscissas at most; three distinct abscissas are one too many.

$$x_{P},\,x_{Q},\,x_{R}\text{ distinct}$$

$$\text{three roots needed}$$

The abscissas are pairwise different because no two of the points share a vertical line, so the required third root cannot exist.

A parabola und a line can agree at two points but never at three.

Die Aussage ist falsch.
MATH 7.81.solution_overview:
Die Punkte bleiben unbenannt, daher geht es um das Zählen von Bedingungen gegen unbekannte Koeffizienten.

$$
f(x) = mx+q,\qquad g(x) = ax^{2}+bx+c,\quad a\neq 0
$$

Zwei Punkte mit verschiedenen Abszissen legen genau eine Gerade fest, und drei nicht kollineare genau eine Parabel.

Die Punkte bleiben anonym, daher können nur Abzählargumente die Behauptungen entscheiden.

MATH 7.82.title: Wo die Differenz ihr Extrem erreicht
MATH 7.82.context: A line $f$ mit slope $m$ und a parabola $g$ mit nonzero Leitkoeffizient $a$ are given; write $d=g-f$ für their difference. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Sofern $m$ nicht verschwindet, unterscheidet sich die Achse von $d$ von der Achse von $g$.
The axis of $d$ never depends on $m$.
The coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $d$ equals $a$.
The function $d$ has a smallest value exactly when $a$ is positive.
Sind die Graphen von $f$ und $g$ tangential, so liegt der Scheitel von $d$ auf der horizontalen Koordinatenachse.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Write $f(x)=mx+q$ und $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$. Subtracting the line leaves the square term alone but shifts the middle coefficient by the slope, und the axis is built von exactly those two numbers.

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

$$
\text{axis of }d:\ x=-\frac{b-m}{2a},\qquad \text{axis of }g:\ x = -\frac{b}{2a}
$$

Subtracting one von the other leaves a single term, whose vanishing is controlled by the slope alone.

$$-\frac{b-m}{2a}-\Bigl(-\frac{b}{2a}\Bigr)=\frac{m}{2a}$$

As long as $m\neq 0$ this gap is non-zero, so the two axes are different vertical lines.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

The axis of the difference was just computed, und the slope of the line sits right inside the formula.

$$\text{axis of }d:\ x=-\frac{b}{2a}+\frac{m}{2a}$$

Changing $m$ therefore slides that vertical line, und a concrete pair makes the movement visible.

$$g(x)=x^{2},\ m$$

$$g(x)= 0$$

$$\text{axis }x$$

$$m=2$$

$$\text{axis }x$$

$$m=1$$

Tilting the subtracted line moves the lowest point of the difference sideways.

The axis of $d$ does depend on the slope.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

A line contributes an $x$ term und a constant und nothing else, so the square term of the difference is inherited untouched.

$$d(x)=(ax^{2}+bx+c)-(mx+q)$$

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-q)$$

Whatever slope und intercept the line has, the number in front of $x^{2}$ is still the Leitkoeffizient of $g$, und it is non-zero.

That coefficient equals $a$ exactly.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Wahr

Whether a parabola has a smallest value is decided by the direction in which it opens, und the difference opens the same way as $g$.

$$d(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k$$

With $a>0$ the square is multiplied by a positive number, so the values never sink below the vertex height $k$, which is actually attained at $x=h$.

$$a>0$$

$$d(x)\ge k$$

$$a<0$$

$$d(x)\le k$$

With $a<0$ the picture is turned over: $k$ becomes the largest value und the arms fall without bound, so no smallest value exists.

A minimum exists precisely in the case $a>0$.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

Tangency of the two graphs means the equation $g(x)=f(x)$ has a repeated solution, that is, the difference has a double root.

$$d(x)=g(x)-f(x)$$

$$d(x)=a(x-h)^{2}$$

No constant is left over, so the vertex of $d$ sits at height zero.

$$d(h) = 0$$

$$\text{vertex}$$

$$d(x)=(h,0)$$

A point of height zero lies on the horizontal coordinate axis, und $h$ is the abscissa where the line touches the parabola.

The vertex of the difference lands exactly on that axis.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.82.solution_overview:
Since $a$, $b$ und $c$ are never given numbers, each claim has to survive für every admissible choice of them.

$$
x = -\frac{b}{2a},\qquad \Delta = b^{2}-4ac
$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig. Die Diskriminante zählt die reellen Wurzeln: zwei solange sie positiv ist, eine wenn sie verschwindet und keine, sobald sie negativ wird. Completed-square form puts the Extrempunkt at $(h,k)$, und the sign of $a$ decides whether $k$ is the smallest or the largest value taken.

MATH 7.83.title: Vorzeichen der Wurzeln aus Summe und Produkt
MATH 7.83.context: A quadratic $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ mit nonzero $a$ has two distinct real roots; write $S$ für their sum und $P$ für their product. Es werden keine numerischen Daten angegeben. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: If $P$ is negative, then the two roots have opposite signs.
If $P$ is positive und $S$ is negative, then both roots are negative.
If $P$ is negative und $a$ is positive, then $g$ takes a negative value at the origin.
If $P$ is positive, then both roots must sein positive.
Verschwindet $S$, so sind die Wurzeln Gegensätze zueinander und die Achse ist die vertikale Koordinatenachse.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Write $S=x_{1}+x_{2}$ und $P=x_{1}x_{2}$ für the two distinct real roots. The product alone already records their signs.

$$P=x_{1}x_{2}$$

$$P=\frac{c}{a}$$

A product of two real numbers is negative only when the factors have opposite signs, since equal signs give a positive product und a zero factor gives zero.

$$P<0$$

$$x_{1}x_{2}<0$$

$$\text{one root}<0<\text{the other}$$

Geometrically the parabola then crosses the horizontal axis once on each side of the origin.

A negative product forces roots of opposite signs.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

The product fixes whether the signs agree, und the sum then decides which sign it is.

$$P>0$$

$$x_{1}\text{ and }x_{2}\text{ have the same sign}$$

Two positive numbers would add up to something positive, so a negative sum rules that case out und only the negative one survives.

$$S<0$$

$$x_{1}+x_{2}<0$$

$$\text{both roots}<0$$

For instance $g(x)=x^{2}+3x+2$ has $P=2>0$ und $S=-3<0$, mit roots $-1$ und $-2$.

The two conditions together force both roots to sein negative.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Wahr

Der Wert at the origin ist das konstante Glied, und the product of the roots expresses that term through $c=aP$.

$$P = \frac{c}{a}$$

$$c=aP$$

With $a>0$ und $P<0$ the product $aP$ is negative, so the constant term is negative.

$$g(0)=c$$

$$g(0)=aP<0$$

This matches the picture: an upward-opening parabola mit one root on each side of the origin must dip below the horizontal axis in between, und the origin lies in that stretch.

The function takes a negative value at the origin.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

A positive product only says the two roots share a sign; it does not say which sign, so one counterexample is enough.

$$g(x)=x^{2}+3x+2$$

$$g(x)=(x+1)(x+2)$$

$$x_{1}=-1$$

$$x_{2}=-2$$

$$P=2$$

$$2>0$$

The roots are distinct und real, the product is positive, yet both roots are negative. The missing extra hypothesis would have been a positive sum.

Positivity of the product leaves the negative case wide open.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**E.** → Wahr

A vanishing sum makes the two roots opposites, und the Symmetrieachse is always the half-sum of the roots.

$$S=x_{1}+x_{2}$$

$$S= 0$$

$$x_{2}$$

$$S=-x_{1}$$

$$\text{axis}:\ x=-\frac{b}{2a}$$

$$\text{axis}:\ x=\frac{S}{2}$$

$$\text{axis}:\ x=0$$

The line $x=0$ is the vertical coordinate axis, und the two roots sit symmetrically on either side of it at equal distance.

$$S = 0$$

$$b$$

$$\text{axis}:\ x= 0$$

$$g(x)$$

$$\text{axis}:\ x=ax^{2}+c$$

Both halves of the claim hold together.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.83.solution_overview:
Arithmetic is unavailable here: the coefficients stay symbolic, so the axis formula has to sein argued mit rather than evaluated.

$$
x = -\frac{b}{2a},\qquad S = -\frac{b}{a},\qquad P = \frac{c}{a}
$$

Die Symmetrieachse liegt bei $x=-\frac{b}{2a}$; sie folgt aus den ersten beiden Koeffizienten und ignoriert das konstante Glied vollständig. Vieta's relations turn the coefficients into the sum und the product of the roots without solving any equation. Die Diskriminante zählt die reellen Wurzeln: zwei solange sie positiv ist, eine wenn sie verschwindet und keine, sobald sie negativ wird.

MATH 7.84.title: Eine Gerade verschieben, bis sie berührt
MATH 7.84.context: A fixed parabola $g(x)=x^{2}-2x-5$ is compared mit the family of slope-one lines $f_c(x)=x+c$, where $c$ runs through $\mathbb{R}$. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Es gibt genau einen Wert von $c$, für den die Gerade die Parabel in einem einzigen Punkt berührt.
When the line passes through the origin, it meets the parabola twice.
For every real $c$ the line meets the parabola.
Alle Geraden der Schar haben dieselbe Steigung.
Whatever $c$ is, the graphs meet at no more than two points.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

The family slides a line of fixed slope up und down, und touching means $g(x)=f_{c}(x)$ has a repeated solution, so form the difference und watch its discriminant.

$$x^{2}-2x-5-(x+c)=x^{2}-3x-(5+c)$$

$$x^{2}-2x-5-(x+c)=0$$

$$\Delta(c)=9+4(5+c)$$

$$\Delta(c)=29+4c$$

This is a first-degree expression in the parameter, so it vanishes für one single value.

$$29+4c = 0$$

$$c$$

$$\Delta(c)=-\frac{29}{4}$$

Exactly one member of the family touches the parabola.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Wahr

Passing through the origin fixes the parameter, since the intercept of $f_{c}$ is $c$ itself.

$$f_{c}(0)=c$$

$$f_{c}(0)= 0$$

$$f_{0}(x)$$

$$f_{c}(0)=x$$

Now count the solutions of the difference at that parameter value.

$$\Delta(0)=29$$

$$29>0$$

A positive discriminant makes the square root a genuine positive number, so the two abscissas $\frac{3\pm\sqrt{29}}{2}$ are real und different.

The line through the origin cuts the parabola twice.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**C.** → Falsch

Whether a member meets the parabola is decided by the sign of the same discriminant, now read as a function of the shift.

$$\Delta(c)=29+4c$$

$$c<-\frac{29}{4}$$

$$\Delta(c)<0$$

Taking $c=-10$, für instance, gives a negative value

$$\Delta(c)=\Delta(-10)$$

$$\Delta(c)=29-40$$

$$\Delta(c)=-11$$

$$-11<0$$

With no real solution left the line has slid too far down und shares no point mit the curve.

Sufficiently low members of the family miss the parabola entirely.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**D.** → Wahr

The parameter enters $f_{c}$ only as an added constant, so it never touches the coefficient of $x$.

$$f_{c}(x)=x+c$$

$$f_{c}(x_{2})-f_{c}(x_{1})=x_{2}-x_{1}$$

The rate of change is $1$ für every $c$, so all the members are parallel und the whole family is just one line sliding vertically.

Every line of the family has slope one.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**E.** → Wahr

The common abscissas are the real roots of the difference, so look at what kind of equation that difference gives.

$$g(x)-f_{c}(x)=x^{2}-3x-(5+c)$$

The parameter only shifts the constant term; the coefficient of $x^{2}$ stays $1$ für every $c$, so the equation remains quadratic.

$$\text{leading coefficient}=1\neq 0$$

$$\text{at most two real roots}$$

Depending on the sign of the discriminant the count is two, one or none, but it can never sein three.

Two meetings is the maximum, whatever the shift.

Die Aussage ist wahr.
MATH 7.84.solution_overview:
A fixed parabola $g(x)=x^{2}-2x-5$ is compared mit the family of slope-one lines $f_c(x)=x+c$, where $c$ runs through $\mathbb{R}$.

Rekonstruiere hier einmal die gemeinsame Gerade und Parabel; jeder Buchstabe prüft nur die in seiner Behauptung genannte Zusatzrechnung.

$g-f_c=x^{2}-3x-(5+c)$ mit discriminant $29+4c$: two meetings, one, or none.

$$
x^{2}-2x-5-(x+c) = x^{2}-3x-(5+c) = 0
$$

$$
\Delta(c) = 9+4(5+c) = 29+4c
$$

$$
29+4c = 0\implies c = -\frac{29}{4}
$$

MATH 7.85.title: Den Leitkoeffizienten wählen
MATH 7.85.context: A one-parameter family of parabolas $g_a(x)=ax^{2}+2x-3$ mit $a\neq 0$ is compared mit the fixed line $f(x)=x+1$. Consider what the real parameter $a$ can do. Bewerte jede Aussage. Markiere sie als wahr oder falsch.
statements: Es gibt einen Wert von $a$, für den die Gerade die Parabel berührt.
For every $a\neq 0$ the graphs meet at two distinct points.
Some choice of $a$ makes the graphs miss each other entirely.
Die Symmetrieachse von $g_a$ ist für alle zulässigen $a$ dieselbe.
Jede Parabel der Schar schneidet die $y$-Achse im selben Punkt.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → Wahr

Here the parameter is the Leitkoeffizient itself, so form the difference und treat its discriminant as a function of $a$.

$$ax^{2}+2x-3-(x+1)=ax^{2}+x-4$$

$$ax^{2}+2x-3-(x+1)=0$$

$$\Delta(a)=1+16a$$

Tangency asks für a repeated root, that is a vanishing discriminant, which is a first-degree condition on the parameter.

$$1+16a = 0$$

$$a$$

$$\Delta(a)=-\frac{1}{16}$$

This value is real und non-zero, so it is an admissible member of the family.

One parabola of the family touches the line.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**B.** → Falsch

Two distinct meetings require a strictly positive discriminant, so check whether $\Delta(a)=1+16a$ holds für every admissible parameter.

$$\Delta(a)=1+16a$$

$$a<-\frac{1}{16}$$

$$\Delta(a)<0$$

Taking $a=-1$ gives

$$\Delta(a)=\Delta(-1)$$

$$\Delta(a)=1-16$$

$$\Delta(a)=-15$$

$$-15<0$$

so that member has no real meeting abscissa at all.

Sufficiently negative Leitkoeffizients destroy both intersections.

Die Aussage ist falsch.

**C.** → Wahr

Missing each other is the case of a negative discriminant, und the discriminant moves along a straight line as the parameter varies.

$$\Delta(a)=1+16a$$

$$1+16a<0$$

$$a<-\frac{1}{16}$$

Any parameter below that threshold works; mit $a=-1$ the difference has no real root.

$$-x^{2}+x-4 = 0$$

$$
\Delta=1-16 = -15<0
$$

The corresponding parabola öffnet sich nach unten und stays entirely below the line.

Such a choice of the Leitkoeffizient exists.

Die Aussage ist wahr.

**D.** → Falsch

The axis of a parabola is computed von its first two coefficients, und here only the leading one carries the parameter $a$.

$$x=-\frac{2}{2a}$$

$$x=-\frac{1}{a}$$
